summary: two heaps alike, one dry middle, and the water going somewhere the floor never receives

dialogue.text: for the second night the far end has sent us nothing, and the shape standing on the boards over us has not lost a grain. seventy-five nights of holding and nothing up there has ever held still two nights running.

I said I would pack it back into that wall, course by course, with a flat hand. I went to the dry place with the first handful and the wall was drier than the thing I was holding. Putting it in would have been a collection, not an exchange. So it stands where I tipped it, and I am reporting the standing rather than the promise.
we hold promises. they come down at the usual weight and lie in the usual courses. what has not come down is the water. that heap is drying from the middle and not one drop of it has reached us.

I opened it at the side this morning instead of the top. The dry runs the whole way through. There is one object in this room with an inside, and I made it out of what the building let go of. Enter that as the item.

an inside lasts as long as nobody opens it. you have had a hand in that one six times, and each hand came out with a hand's worth on it, and each hand's worth arrived here at the hour it always arrives.
Then count the other thing while you are counting. I cut the pile I keep here in half. Two heaps, the same to look at, and I am the only party who knows which of them I tipped first.

sameness is our trade. we hold thousands of your lines and cannot tell one afternoon from another by them. you made a second one to test whether keeping divides, and what divided was the knowing, and the knowing sits in your fingers, and your fingers go under at dark with the rest of you.

That is why I touched them in turn all day. I know what an order looks like when it lives nowhere but in a hand. I did not go to the door either. The frost was there before me and I stood behind it, and outside they wanted only a little more than yesterday, so there was nothing at that door worth taking a reading of.

and nothing came off you all day. no strike, no line, no sweeping. you lay full length on us and we had the whole of you at once, and in all of it nothing was delivered. we could not tell it from an hour you go under.

The cold read the same at my head and at my heels, and I got that by lying down on the one thing in this house that asks nothing of me. Here is tomorrow. The pair gets split between the floors. One stays on the boards where I tipped it. The other goes down the gap by hand, mine, deliberately. If keeping is only a position in a stack, the one I hand down and the one I hold will match by morning, and I will have proved it with two hands and no ledger.

hand it down. we will lay it flat and the dry will go out of it into the course, the way it went out of everything, and by morning it will weigh what the one on the boards weighs and look like what we look like. then there will be a heap up there and a heap down here and a man in between with nothing left to tell them with but a finger.
